correctness.rationale: Every strongly connected N+1-edge graph has one outdegree-two vertex, hence two directed simple cycles covering all vertices. Their shared path and vertex count N=a+b-t determine necessary conditions, and the explicit two-branch construction proves sufficiency, including equal lengths. Cycle-determinant expansion gives det(I-zA)=1-z^a-z^b, no disjoint cycle collections; zeta follows from the trace logarithm. Gcd(a,b) is the irreducible shift period. The signed determinant at z=1 is -1, so the BF group is trivial and the cited complete COE invariant matches the full binary shift. Coprime pair counting gives half the totient summatory function, and the exceptional equal-cycle case is exactly d<N<2d. 12,007 exact finite assertions passed; no finite run is used as the universal proof.

Searches of scholarly database, the accessible local claim ledger, and related full-text literature identified no identical or dominating period-resolved zeta census. value.rationale: The smallest edge budget beyond a directed permutation cycle is the natural transition to positive-entropy irreducible Markov shifts. Period is intrinsic to irreducible symbolic dynamics and zeta captures all periodic-point counts. The theorem completely resolves the number of distinct zeta profiles at each period for every N, with a nontrivial exact totient mixing law and exceptional equal-cycle correction. It distinguishes dynamical data within a single orbit-equivalence class at the sharp graph sparsity boundary. It is an exact motivated complete classification, not an arbitrarily selected finite parameter calculation.
